problems.title: 1. LRU Cache with TTL & Generics
problems.problemStatement: Design and implement a thread-safe, fixed-capacity Least Recently Used (LRU) Cache supporting get(key) and put(key, value, [ttl]) in strict O(1) time complexity. When the cache hits capacity, the least recently accessed item must be evicted.
extensions: Time-To-Live (TTL) auto-expiration per key
Generic templated types for Key and Value
Thread-safe reads/writes with mutex locking
dataStructuresUsed: std::unordered_map (Hash Table mapping Key -> Node pointer for O(1) lookups)
Custom Doubly Linked List (Head = Most Recently Used, Tail = Least Recently Used for O(1) removals and insertions)
designPatterns: Composition Pattern (combining Hash Map with Doubly Linked List)
RAII & Smart Pointer management (std::shared_ptr)
problems.spaceComplexity: O(Capacity)
edgeCasesHandled: Key lookup when key has expired via TTL (lazy eviction on get)
Updating value of an already existing key without increasing cache size
Evicting strictly from tail while cleaning up map references
Capacity initialized to 1 or small constraints
Concurrent multi-threaded access without race conditions

problems.title: 2. Multi-Floor Parking Lot System
problems.problemStatement: Design a multi-floor parking lot system supporting diverse vehicle types (Motorbike, Car, Truck, EV Car) with automated spot matching, entry ticket issuance, dynamic parking fee calculation on exit, and pluggable slot allocation strategies.
extensions: Slot allocation strategy (Nearest-first, Cheapest-first)
Dynamic fee calculation based on vehicle type and duration
EV Charging spot integration
Support for multiple entry and exit gates
dataStructuresUsed: std::vector for hierarchical floors and spot collections
std::unordered_map for active ticket tracking and O(1) ticket checkout lookups
designPatterns: Strategy Pattern: Spot Allocation (NearestFirstParkingStrategy) and Pricing (HourlyFeeStrategy)
Factory / Polymorphism: Vehicle and ParkingSpot class hierarchies
Single Responsibility Principle: Clear separation between spot, floor, ticket, and lot controller

timeComplexity.parkVehicle: O(F * S) where F is floors and S is spots per floor
timeComplexity.unparkVehicle: O(1) ticket lookup and spot release

problems.spaceComplexity: O(Total Spots + Active Tickets)
edgeCasesHandled: No spots available for a specific vehicle category
Invalid or expired ticket ID verification on checkout
Truck or large vehicle attempting to park in small/compact spots
Zero-minute or instant exit charged with minimum 1-hour base rate

problems.title: 3. N x N Tic-Tac-Toe with O(1) Win Check & Undo
problems.problemStatement: Build an extensible N x N Tic-Tac-Toe game supporting 2 or more players. Every move must be strictly validated, and win/draw condition must be evaluated in O(1) time without looping through the entire grid. Supports an Undo move capability.
extensions: Arbitrary N x N board size
Undo functionality using move command history stack
Pluggable player strategies (Human vs Bot/AI player)
dataStructuresUsed: std::vector<int> for rowCounts and colCounts to evaluate win status in O(1)
int diagCount and antiDiagCount tracking diagonal sums
std::stack<Move> for undo history
designPatterns: Strategy Pattern (Player interface with HumanPlayer vs BotPlayer)
Command / Memento Pattern (storing Move history on stack for undo operations)
problems.spaceComplexity: O(N^2) for grid and O(Total Moves) for undo stack
edgeCasesHandled: Placing a piece on an already occupied cell
Out of bounds coordinates validation
Board full detection (Draw condition) when total moves equal N*N
Invoking Undo on an empty board

problems.title: 4. Library Management System
problems.problemStatement: Design a system where members can search, checkout, return, and reserve books. A book can have multiple physical copies (BookItems). Overdue returns trigger automated fine calculations, and returning a reserved copy immediately notifies the waiting member.
extensions: Search catalog by Title, Author, or ISBN
Observer pattern notifying members on reservation availability
Configurable checkout limits and daily overdue fine calculations
dataStructuresUsed: std::unordered_map for indexing books by ISBN, Author, and Title
std::queue<std::shared_ptr<Member>> for FIFO reservation waitlist per book copy
designPatterns: Observer Pattern: Notifying waiting members when a book item is checked in
Domain Separation: Book (Metadata) vs BookItem (Physical Copy with Barcode and State)
problems.spaceComplexity: O(Total Books + Total Members + Active Loans)
edgeCasesHandled: Member reaching maximum allowed active checkouts (e.g., max 5 books)
Calculating daily compounding fines on delayed returns past due date
Transitioning book status to RESERVED when a waitlist exists rather than AVAILABLE
Handling concurrent reservation queue order

problems.title: 5. Vending Machine (State Pattern)
problems.problemStatement: Implement a vending machine capable of holding inventory, accepting coins/cash, dispensing requested products, returning remaining change, and handling cancellations with a full refund. The machine must enforce valid state transitions without nested conditionals.
extensions: State Pattern implementation (IdleState, HasMoneyState, DispenseState)
Out-of-stock and inventory management
Transaction cancellation with coin return
dataStructuresUsed: std::unordered_map<std::string, Item> for product inventory by aisle code
designPatterns: State Pattern: Encapsulating state-dependent behavior in dedicated State classes
Polymorphism: Eliminating nested if/switch statements
problems.spaceComplexity: O(Total Products in Inventory)
edgeCasesHandled: Selecting an item with insufficient deposited balance
Selecting an item that is out of stock (quantity = 0)
Attempting to dispense when no money was inserted
Cancelling transaction while dispensing (strictly prohibited by state machine)
Accurate change calculation and balance reset

setName: Set 2: Intermediate LLD Problems (Splitwise & Elevator System)

problems.title: 6. Splitwise (Expense Sharing & Debt Simplification)
problems.problemStatement: Design an expense sharing system like Splitwise where users can create groups, log shared expenses across multiple split types (EQUAL, EXACT, PERCENT), and calculate net balances between users. The system must support debt simplification to minimize the total number of settling transactions.
extensions: Debt Simplification Algorithm using Greedy Min-Heap & Max-Heap
Multiple Split Strategies (Equal, Exact amount, Percentage share)
Audit trail & immutable expense history tracking
Floating-point roundoff discrepancy handling (penny balancing)
dataStructuresUsed: std::unordered_map for nested 2D user balance sheets (UserA -> UserB -> Net Balance)
std::priority_queue (Max-Heap for Creditors, Min-Heap for Debtors) to simplify circular cash flows in O(N log N) time
designPatterns: Strategy Pattern: Expense validation and split calculation (EqualSplitStrategy, ExactSplitStrategy, PercentSplitStrategy)
Factory Pattern: Creating split objects dynamically based on expense input payload
Observer Pattern (Extensible): Event hooks notifying users when debts are updated or settled

timeComplexity.addExpense: O(M) where M is the number of users involved in the split
timeComplexity.simplifyDebts: O(N log N) where N is the total number of unique users with non-zero net balances
timeComplexity.showBalances: O(N^2) in worst case pairwise display, O(1) per direct lookup

problems.spaceComplexity: O(U^2) where U is total registered users (pair-wise ledger representation)
edgeCasesHandled: Percentage splits not adding up to 100.0%
Exact amount splits not summing exactly to the total expense amount
Handling pennies and fractional divisions (e.g. 100 split 3 ways)
Self-payments or users owing money to themselves
Circular debt cycles (A owes B, B owes C, C owes A) simplified down to direct settlements

problems.title: 7. Multi-Car Elevator Management System (SCAN/LOOK Algorithm)
problems.problemStatement: Design a centralized elevator dispatch and control system managing N floors and M elevator cars. The system must process external hallway requests (Up/Down from floor buttons) and internal car destination buttons, scheduling cars efficiently using the SCAN/LOOK elevator disk algorithm while handling overload constraints and direction reversals.
extensions: SCAN / LOOK directional elevator scheduling algorithm
State Pattern for elevator car lifecycle transitions
Nearest-Car-Same-Direction dispatching heuristic
Weight capacity limit and overload handling
dataStructuresUsed: std::set / Sorted Arrays for Floor requests (separating UP and DOWN stops)
Priority Queues / Directional vectors for order-preserving passenger pickups
designPatterns: State Pattern: Elevator car lifecycle states (Idle, MovingUp, MovingDown, StoppedAtFloor)
Strategy Pattern: Elevator dispatching heuristics (NearestCarDispatchStrategy vs RoundRobinStrategy)
Dispatcher / Mediator Pattern: Central controller coordinating communication between floor buttons and elevator car hardware

timeComplexity.pressButton: O(log F) where F is the number of building floors
timeComplexity.dispatchNextMove: O(1) step simulation per elevator car
timeComplexity.findBestElevator: O(M) where M is the total number of elevator cars

problems.spaceComplexity: O(M * F) across all elevator stop targets
edgeCasesHandled: Car reaches top or bottom floor boundary and safely reverses direction
Overload sensor trip preventing doors from closing and car from moving
Simultaneous hallway button presses on identical floors from multiple users
Assigning idle cars closest to pickup requests

setName: Set 2: Advanced LLD Problems (BookMyShow & ATM System)

problems.title: 8. BookMyShow / Movie Booking System (Concurrency & Seat Locking)
problems.problemStatement: Design a movie ticket booking platform supporting hierarchical entities (Cities -> Theatres -> Screens -> Shows -> Seats). The system must allow users to view available seats, temporarily lock seats for a checkout window (e.g. 5-10 minutes), process payments, and confirm bookings. Two concurrent users must never be able to book or lock the exact same seat simultaneously.
extensions: Temporary Seat Locking with TTL timeout auto-release
Thread-safe concurrent seat selection using mutexes / locks
Optimistic status checking (AVAILABLE -> TEMPORARILY_LOCKED -> BOOKED)
Dynamic ticket pricing by seat tier (Silver, Gold, Platinum)
dataStructuresUsed: std::unordered_map for fast show lookups and seat index mapping
std::mutex for fine-grained per-show seat state synchronization
std::chrono timestamps to validate lock expiration
designPatterns: State Pattern / Status Enum: Transitioning seat lifecycle (Available -> Locked -> Booked)
Strategy Pattern (Extensible): Seat pricing tiers and promotional discounts
Repository / Facade Pattern: CinemaBookingService exposing clean APIs to clients

timeComplexity.getSeatLayout: O(S) where S is the number of seats in the screen
timeComplexity.temporaryLockSeats: O(K) where K is the number of seats requested to lock
timeComplexity.confirmBooking: O(K) seat status update to BOOKED

problems.spaceComplexity: O(Shows * Seats + Active Bookings)
edgeCasesHandled: Race condition: Two users hitting 'Book' for Seat A1 at the exact same millisecond
Expired temporary locks automatically rolling back to AVAILABLE state
User abandoning payment screen after locking seats
Partial seat locking failure (if 3 out of 4 seats are locked, roll back the entire transaction atomically)

problems.title: 9. ATM (State Pattern & Cash Dispenser Chain of Responsibility)
problems.problemStatement: Design an Automated Teller Machine (ATM) that supports card insertion, PIN verification, balance inquiries, cash withdrawal, and card ejection. Cash withdrawals must dispense the optimal mix of currency denominations (Rs 2000, 500, 200, 100) using the Chain of Responsibility pattern. The ATM must enforce strict state transitions using the State Pattern.
extensions: State Pattern (IdleState, HasCardState, PinVerifiedState, DispenseState)
Chain of Responsibility Pattern for Cash Dispensing denomination cascade
Insufficient cash in ATM vaults error handling
Transaction cancellation with safe card ejection
dataStructuresUsed: Linked Chain pointers for Dispenser Handlers (2000 -> 500 -> 200 -> 100)
Hash Map for user bank account database lookup and balances
designPatterns: State Pattern: Encapsulating state transitions across ATM lifecycle
Chain of Responsibility Pattern: Sequentially delegating cash dispensation across note handlers

timeComplexity.withdrawCash: O(D) where D is the number of supported currency denominations

problems.spaceComplexity: O(1) state variables and vault denomination tracking
edgeCasesHandled: Withdrawal amount that cannot be fulfilled by available note denominations (e.g. Rs 50)
ATM vault running out of high-denomination bills, cascading to lower bills
Entering incorrect PIN
Attempting to withdraw cash while in IdleState without card insertion

setName: Set 2: Classic Board Game LLD Problems (Snake & Ladder & Chess)

problems.title: 10. Snake and Ladder Game
problems.problemStatement: Design a multiplayer Snake and Ladder game supporting N players and a board of arbitrary size (default 100). The game should simulate dice rolls, handle jumps across snakes (sliding down) and ladders (climbing up), and enforce that a player must land exactly on the final winning square to win.
extensions: Multiple dice simulation (e.g. 2 dice producing numbers from 2 to 12)
Configurable board dimension (10x10, 8x8, etc.) and custom jump configurations
Difficulty modes (e.g. dynamic snake placements, extra turn on rolling max dice value)
Consecutive max roll penalties (rolling three 6s cancels the turn)
dataStructuresUsed: std::unordered_map<int, int> for O(1) jump lookup mapping start square to destination square
std::queue<std::shared_ptr<Player>> for round-robin player turn management
std::vector for dice collection
designPatterns: Strategy Pattern: Dice rolling behavior (StandardRandomDice vs RiggedTestDice)
Composition Pattern: Board holding jumps, Game holding players, board, and dice
State / Turn Management: Queue-based rotation maintaining active and finished players

timeComplexity.rollDice: O(D) where D is the number of dice rolled
timeComplexity.executeTurn: O(1) position lookup and jump resolution
timeComplexity.fullGameSimulation: O(K * P) where P is players and K is average turns to reach 100

problems.spaceComplexity: O(B + P) where B is total board squares and P is total players
edgeCasesHandled: Player roll overshooting the final square (move rejected, player stays put)
Landing on the head of a snake or base of a ladder triggers immediate position update
Preventing infinite loop cycles (e.g. ladder bottom at a snake tail and vice versa)
Handling 1 player finishing while continuing game for remaining ranks (1st, 2nd place)

problems.title: 11. Chess Game (Object-Oriented Move Rules & Check Detection)
problems.problemStatement: Design a 2-player Chess game on an 8x8 board. Each piece type (King, Queen, Rook, Bishop, Knight, Pawn) must enforce its individual valid movement rules. The board must prevent moving through intermediate occupied squares for non-knights, handle check detection against the King, and track turn history with an undo mechanism.
extensions: Checkmate and Stalemate detection
Move history stack for full Undo / Redo functionality
Special rules: Castling, En Passant, and Pawn Promotion
FEN (Forsyth-Edwards Notation) board state serialization
dataStructuresUsed: 2D 8x8 array / vector of std::shared_ptr<Piece> representing the board squares
std::stack<Move> for tracking move histories and supporting reversible undo actions
std::pair<int, int> coordinate mappings
designPatterns: Polymorphism & Strategy: Piece abstract base class with individual `canMove()` implementations
Command Pattern: Move object encapsulating source, destination, captured piece, and reversible state
Facade Pattern: ChessGame class orchestrating turn switches, validation, and check checks

timeComplexity.validateMove: O(1) geometric step check + O(8) max path collision check
timeComplexity.isKingInCheck: O(64) scan of opponent pieces attacking king coordinates

problems.spaceComplexity: O(1) fixed 64 board squares + O(M) for move history stack
edgeCasesHandled: Pawn moving forward vs capturing diagonally
Knight jumping over pieces while other pieces are blocked by obstacles
Preventing friendly fire (cannot capture a piece of the same color)
Moving out of turn (White plays first, strictly alternating turns)
Undoing moves restores any captured piece back to its exact square

setName: Set 2: Enterprise Architectural LLD Problems (Notification System & Logger Framework)

problems.title: 12. Multi-Channel Notification System
problems.problemStatement: Design an extensible notification service capable of dispatching notifications across multiple channels (Email, SMS, Push). Users can configure their preferred delivery channels per notification type (Transactional, Promotional). The architecture must follow Open/Closed Principle (OCP) so that introducing a new channel (e.g. WhatsApp, Slack) requires zero modifications to existing sender logic.
extensions: Rate limiting per channel and per user (preventing notification spam)
Template engine interpolation for localized dynamic messages
Retry mechanics with fallback channels (if Push fails, fallback to SMS)
Batching and async delivery queue integration
dataStructuresUsed: std::unordered_set<ChannelType> for user delivery preferences
std::unordered_map<ChannelType, std::shared_ptr<NotificationSender>> for Strategy / Factory registration lookup
std::vector<std::shared_ptr<NotificationObserver>> for event listener dispatch
designPatterns: Strategy Pattern: Encapsulating transport protocols (EmailSender, SMSSender, PushSender)
Factory Pattern: NotificationSenderFactory to resolve the right channel sender dynamically
Observer Pattern: Event publishers notifying subscribers who evaluate user preferences and trigger sends

timeComplexity.sendNotification: O(C) where C is the number of enabled channels for the recipient
timeComplexity.registerChannel: O(1) insertion into the strategy registry
timeComplexity.updatePreference: O(1) hash set lookup and update

problems.spaceComplexity: O(U * C) where U is registered users and C is channel preferences
edgeCasesHandled: User disabling all notification channels (graceful skip without throwing errors)
Handling network transport failures in individual channels without breaking others
Dispatching promotional alerts only to channels opted-in by user preferences
Extending new channels at runtime without touching dispatch orchestration

problems.title: 13. Logger Framework (Log Levels, Multi-Sink & Chain of Responsibility)
problems.problemStatement: Design a centralized, thread-safe Logger Framework supporting multiple log levels (DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR). The system must route log messages through a Chain of Responsibility where each logger sink (ConsoleLogger, FileLogger, DatabaseLogger) evaluates severity thresholds and writes to its destination. The main logger must follow the Singleton pattern.
extensions: Async background batch logging using worker threads and lock-free queues
Configurable log formatting patterns ([TIMESTAMP] [LEVEL] [THREAD_ID] - Message)
Log rotation policies (Size-based or Daily file rolling)
Dynamic log level modification at runtime without restarting the application
dataStructuresUsed: Linked pointers linking successive AbstractLogger handlers in the responsibility chain
std::mutex ensuring thread safety during concurrent file/console I/O operations
std::chrono for ISO-8601 millisecond timestamp generation
designPatterns: Singleton Pattern: Global thread-safe LoggerManager access point
Chain of Responsibility Pattern: Filtering severity and cascading messages down the logger chain
Strategy / Adapter Pattern (Extensible): Pluggable Sink Formatters and Output streams

timeComplexity.log: O(N) where N is the depth of the logging chain (typically 3-4 sinks)
timeComplexity.filterCheck: O(1) integer comparison of log levels

problems.spaceComplexity: O(1) persistent state in heap memory for sink references
edgeCasesHandled: Filtering out lower severity logs when log level is set higher (e.g. DEBUG message ignored when root is INFO)
Simultaneous logs written from multiple background threads without interleaving characters
Graceful handling when File sink disk buffer is full or DB sink is temporarily disconnected
Cascading execution: A severe ERROR message writing to Console, File, AND Database sinks simultaneously

setName: Set 2: Infrastructure & Distributed LLD Problems (Rate Limiter & Pub-Sub Queue)

problems.title: 14. Multi-Strategy Client Rate Limiter
problems.problemStatement: Design a thread-safe, client-specific Rate Limiter that restricts the rate of requests per user or IP address (e.g. 5 requests per second). The system must employ the Strategy Pattern so that rate-limiting algorithms (Token Bucket, Sliding Window Log, Fixed Window Counter) can be swapped seamlessly at runtime without altering client integration code.
extensions: Dynamic tier-based quotas (Free tier = 10 req/min, Premium tier = 1000 req/min)
Sliding Window Counter algorithm to conserve memory
Distributed synchronization support (Redis cluster backend pluggability)
Configurable penalty windows and HTTP 429 Too Many Requests response headers
dataStructuresUsed: std::unordered_map<std::string, ClientState> for per-client bucket/window tracking
std::deque<std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point> for sliding window timestamp logs
std::mutex for synchronizing concurrent access across multiple worker threads
designPatterns: Strategy Pattern: RateLimitingAlgorithm interface implemented by TokenBucket, SlidingWindowLog, and FixedWindow
Factory Pattern: Dynamically creating and configuring algorithm instances
Decorator / Interceptor Pattern: Middleware wrapping HTTP/RPC controllers

timeComplexity.allowRequest (Token Bucket): O(1) time calculation and token increment
timeComplexity.allowRequest (Sliding Window Log): O(K) where K is number of expired requests popped from front of deque
timeComplexity.allowRequest (Fixed Window): O(1) counter check and modulo reset

problems.spaceComplexity: O(U * K) where U is active clients and K is window request history
edgeCasesHandled: Burst traffic handling up to maximum bucket capacity
Fixed-window boundary traffic spikes (double allowance across window edges)
Multi-threaded concurrent requests hitting the limiter for the same user ID simultaneously
Time drift and leap clock shifts handled via std::chrono::steady_clock

problems.title: 15. In-Memory Pub-Sub & Message Broker (Kafka-style)
problems.problemStatement: Design a high-throughput, thread-safe in-memory publish-subscribe message broker. The architecture must feature partitioned Topics, persistent append-only in-memory storage, multiple independent Consumer Groups, and dedicated offset tracking so consumers can read and acknowledge messages independently at their own pace.
extensions: Partition key hashing (e.g. key % partitions to preserve strict ordering)
Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) integration on consumer retry exhaustion
Consumer Group automatic rebalancing logic
Message TTL expiration and memory retention cleanup
dataStructuresUsed: std::vector<Message> representing append-only partition commit logs
std::unordered_map<std::string, std::atomic<int>> for per-group offset tracking
std::condition_variable and std::mutex for non-busy waiting thread synchronization
designPatterns: Publish-Subscribe / Observer Pattern: Decoupling producers from message consumers
Producer-Consumer Pattern: Blocking concurrent queues with conditional wait-notify
Broker / Mediator Pattern: Central coordinator managing topic lifecycles and partition assignment

timeComplexity.publishMessage: O(1) append to vector partition log

problems.spaceComplexity: O(Total Messages Retained across all Partitions)
edgeCasesHandled: Slow consumer falling behind fast producers without blocking message arrival
Consumer requesting an offset that has not yet been produced (graceful wait)
Zero active consumers at the time of publish (messages remain persistent in log)
Thread contention between concurrent publishers targeting the same topic

setName: Set 3: Application & Workflow LLD Problems (Text Editor & Food Delivery)

problems.title: 16. Text Editor with Undo / Redo (Command & Memento)
problems.problemStatement: Design an in-memory Text Editor supporting operations like inserting text, deleting characters/ranges, and navigating document state. The architecture must feature robust Undo and Redo operations using the Command and Memento design patterns, ensuring that modifying the document after undoing actions safely clears the redo history stack.
extensions: Cursor-based navigation and selection ranges
Clipboard support (Copy, Cut, Paste commands)
Macro recording (Batch command execution)
Piece Table or Rope data structure optimization for large-scale documents
dataStructuresUsed: std::string representing the active document buffer
std::stack<std::shared_ptr<Command>> for undoHistory and redoHistory
designPatterns: Command Pattern: Encapsulating edit actions as executable/reversible Command objects
Memento Pattern: Capturing and restoring internal state snapshots or delta changes
Invoker / Client Pattern: TextEditor acting as the invoker executing commands on the Document receiver

timeComplexity.insertText: O(N) where N is the length of text shifted in buffer
timeComplexity.undo / redo: O(1) stack pop and reverse execution

problems.spaceComplexity: O(M * S) where M is total historical commands and S is average payload size
edgeCasesHandled: Calling Undo when the undo stack is empty
Calling Redo when no prior undo was performed or redo stack has been invalidated
Executing a new edit action while having pending redos (must purge redo stack)
Deleting more characters than currently present in the document buffer

problems.title: 17. Food Delivery System (Swiggy / Zomato Architecture)
problems.problemStatement: Design a food ordering and delivery management system like Swiggy. The system handles Restaurants, dynamic Menus, Customer Carts, and Order checkouts. Once placed, an order transitions through distinct stages (PLACED -> PREPARING -> OUT_FOR_DELIVERY -> DELIVERED) using the State Pattern, dispatches nearest active Delivery Partners using the Strategy Pattern, and emits live status changes to customers using the Observer Pattern.
extensions: Dynamic surge pricing and delivery fee calculation
Restaurant operational hours & item inventory stock validation
Delivery partner batch routing (multi-order pickup)
Customer cancellation policies per state transition
dataStructuresUsed: std::unordered_map for indexing restaurants, menu items, delivery partners, and orders
std::vector<OrderItem> for shopping cart contents
Euclidean / Haversine distance coordinates struct for geospatial distance calculations
designPatterns: State Pattern: OrderState interface (PlacedState, PreparingState, OutForDeliveryState, DeliveredState)
Strategy Pattern: DeliveryMatchingStrategy (NearestPartnerStrategy vs HighestRatedPartnerStrategy)
Observer Pattern: Notifying customers and delivery apps whenever order state updates

timeComplexity.placeOrder: O(Items) cart validation and total sum calculation
timeComplexity.matchDeliveryPartner: O(P) where P is the count of available delivery partners

problems.spaceComplexity: O(Restaurants + Menus + Active Orders + Partners)
edgeCasesHandled: Placing an order when all delivery partners are currently busy/offline
Attempting to cancel an order after it has already entered PREPARING or OUT_FOR_DELIVERY
Ordering items across two different restaurants inside the same cart (disallowed)
Customer notification on out-of-delivery transit confirmation

setName: Set 4: Multi-Threading & Concurrency LLD Problems (Thread-Safe TTL Cache & Task Scheduler)

problems.title: 18. Thread-Safe Cache with TTL & Active Cleanup Worker
problems.problemStatement: Design a high-concurrency, thread-safe in-memory cache supporting generic keys and values with individual Time-To-Live (TTL) expiration. Multiple worker threads must be able to read concurrently without contention using Read-Write locks (std::shared_mutex). The cache must support both passive eviction (on get) and active periodic background cleanup to reclaim memory without CPU busy-waiting.
extensions: ReadWriteLock pattern (concurrent shared readers, exclusive writer)
Dedicated background cleanup thread using condition variables
Configurable eviction policy (LRU / LFU fallback when memory limit hits)
Graceful lifecycle shutdown via RAII destructor stopping background threads
dataStructuresUsed: std::unordered_map<K, CacheEntry> for primary key-value and expiry tracking
std::shared_mutex for Reader-Writer locking (std::shared_lock vs std::unique_lock)
std::condition_variable_any and std::atomic<bool> for background thread synchronization
designPatterns: Read-Write Lock Pattern: Maximizing read throughput in read-heavy caching workloads
Active Object / Daemon Worker Pattern: Background thread handling memory hygiene independently
RAII Pattern: Thread joining and lock lifetime management scoped to object lifespan

timeComplexity.get: O(1) average hash lookup under shared reader lock
timeComplexity.put: O(1) insertion under exclusive write lock
timeComplexity.cleanupCycle: O(N) periodic scan of all entries to evict expired keys

problems.spaceComplexity: O(Total Active Keys)
edgeCasesHandled: Lazy/Passive eviction on get() when a key has expired before the background thread wakes up
Updating an existing key's value and extending its TTL safely under an exclusive lock
Clean shutdown avoiding deadlocks or thread leaks on cache destruction
Zero or negative TTL values handled gracefully

problems.title: 19. Priority Task Scheduler & Job Runner
problems.problemStatement: Design a multi-threaded Task Scheduler capable of executing one-off tasks at a designated future timestamp, recurring cron-like periodic tasks, and prioritizing tasks based on explicit priority weights. The system must use a thread pool of worker threads and coordinate tasks using a min-heap priority queue without spinning CPU cycles.
extensions: Recurring execution intervals (auto-rescheduling recurring jobs on completion)
Priority tie-breaking (Higher priority executed first if timestamps match)
Dynamic task cancellation using TaskId handles
Configurable worker thread pool size
dataStructuresUsed: std::priority_queue with custom comparator ordering by execution time then priority
std::vector<std::thread> for the worker thread pool
std::condition_variable and std::mutex for timed waiting and thread dispatch
designPatterns: Thread Pool Pattern: Fixed pool of worker threads consuming a concurrent priority work queue
Command Pattern: Encapsulating tasks and their execution callbacks as callable objects
Producer-Consumer Pattern: Scheduler pushes delayed tasks; worker threads consume when ready

timeComplexity.scheduleTask: O(log N) insertion into priority queue min-heap
timeComplexity.cancelTask: O(1) flag update on task metadata

problems.spaceComplexity: O(Total Pending Tasks) in heap memory
edgeCasesHandled: Worker waking up early when a newer task with an earlier timestamp is submitted
Empty task queue state handling without thread termination
Recurring task rescheduling accurately based on last scheduled time to prevent drift
Clean shutdown draining pending tasks or terminating workers gracefully

setName: Set 5: Financial, Geospatial & Advanced Concurrent LLD Problems

problems.title: 20. Digital Payment Wallet with Idempotency
problems.problemStatement: Design a digital payment wallet service where users can add funds and transfer balances atomically to other users. The service must guarantee strict idempotency: if network drops trigger identical duplicate transfer requests with the same Idempotency-Key, money must never be deducted twice. Each operation must generate an immutable audit transaction record.
extensions: Distributed lock integration and TTL-backed idempotency cache
Multi-currency support with dynamic FX conversion rates
Two-phase commit simulation (Hold funds -> Settle / Refund)
Daily transfer velocity limits and fraud trigger thresholds
dataStructuresUsed: std::unordered_map<std::string, WalletAccount> for user wallets
std::unordered_map<std::string, TransactionResult> for Idempotency Key state store
std::vector<TransactionRecord> for immutable append-only ledger audit trail
std::mutex and std::lock to atomically lock source and destination accounts without deadlocks
designPatterns: Command / Transaction Script Pattern: Encapsulating credit, debit, and transfer operations
Idempotency Cache Pattern: Intercepting incoming requests via unique client transaction tokens
State / Status Pattern: Transaction states (PENDING, SUCCESS, FAILED, DUPLICATE_BLOCKED)

timeComplexity.transferFunds: O(1) account lookup and atomic balance updates
timeComplexity.getTransactionHistory: O(H) where H is the user's historical transaction count

problems.spaceComplexity: O(Users + Total Transactions + Active Idempotency Keys)
edgeCasesHandled: Duplicate API retry with identical Idempotency-Key returns cached original response without moving funds
Insufficient balance in sender's account aborts cleanly without state corruption
Transferring funds to non-existent recipient account rolls back instantly
Self-transfer attempt rejected immediately

problems.title: 21. Ride-Sharing System (Uber / Ola LLD)
problems.problemStatement: Design a ride-sharing dispatch service like Uber where riders request rides between locations, the system matches the closest active driver, calculates fares dynamically using pricing strategies (Base rate + Surge pricing multiplier), manages state machine transitions (REQUESTED -> ACCEPTED -> ONGOING -> COMPLETED), and aggregates 5-star ratings.
extensions: Dynamic surge pricing algorithm based on localized demand vs driver supply
Geospatial driver matching (Euclidean / KD-Tree / QuadTree indexing)
Ride cancellation policies and rider/driver cancellation fee penalties
Driver rating aggregation and status validation

Geospatial Coordinates struct (x, y) with distance calculation heuristics
std::vector<int> for driver historical rating storage
designPatterns: State Pattern: Ride lifecycle state transitions (RequestedState, AcceptedState, OngoingState, CompletedState)
Strategy Pattern: Pricing calculation (StandardPricingStrategy vs SurgePricingStrategy)
Observer Pattern: Emitting trip status alerts and live driver coordinates to the rider app

problems.title: 22. Concurrent Splitwise (Fine-Grained Locking & Deadlock Avoidance)
problems.problemStatement: Extend the Splitwise expense management engine to handle hundreds of concurrent user requests updating shared expenses and pairwise balances simultaneously without race conditions, corrupted double-counts, or thread deadlocks. Fine-grained locking must be enforced using strict lock ordering mechanisms.
extensions: Deadlock avoidance using std::lock across multi-user balance sheet locks
Concurrent expense posting across shared group ledgers
Thread-safe snapshotting for balance queries without blocking incoming writes indefinitely
Pairwise balance reconciliation with atomic floating-point math

Fine-Grained Locking Pattern: Locking only affected users rather than the entire database/ledger
